angle_name: Signed largest-prime Buchstab contraction in the canonical window
mechanism: Put ℓ(q)=Li(q)−Li(q−1) and a(q)=1_{q prime}−ℓ(q). Exactly rewrite S_y(u)=Σ_{d≤y}μ(d)R(⌊u/d⌋)=Σ_{n≤u}a(n)M(min(y,⌊u/n⌋)). Do not estimate M. Expand it by the exact largest-prime identity Σ_{m≤z,P⁺(m)>v}μ(m)w(m)=−Σ_{v<p≤z}Σ_{r≤z/p,P⁺(r)<p}μ(r)w(pr). Thus each squarefree integer occupies one largest-prime cell and retains the sign μ(pr)=−μ(r). Packetize p dyadically and subtract the ℓ-integral inside each packet before taking any norm. Seek a scale-uniform spectral gap for this centered signed Buchstab operator in the one-sided canonical-window L² norm. Iterating the gap down the largest-prime tree would control the zero-frequency component; the nonzero window frequencies are already elementary: on I=[y²+y,(y+1)²−1], ΔS_y(n)=−μ(n)1_{P⁺(n)>y}−Σ_{d|n,d≤y}μ(d)ℓ(n/d), so |ΔS_y(n)|≪τ(n), and discrete Poincaré plus τ(n)≪εn^ε gives the required x^{1+ε} bound for S−its window mean.
new_leverage: This uses the opening explicitly left by obstacle 9: an exact signed renewal, based on μ(pr)=−μ(r), rather than an absolute-value hyperbola induction. Unique largest-prime ownership replaces the false bounded-fiber transfer of obstacle 2. The canonical backward average supplies the Hilbert norm in which a genuine operator spectral gap can be sought, while the Wigert jumps are confined to an already-controlled nonzero-frequency term.
target_estimate: For X=(y+1)²−1, W=y+1, and dyadic prime packets P, let B_P(u) be the centered largest-prime cell obtained from the exact expansion above: the sum over p∈(P,2P], r≤u/p, P⁺(r)

obstacle_positions.1: No Mertens moment is inserted and no absolute Cauchy–Schwarz over d is used; M is expanded exactly into signed largest-prime cells before squaring.
obstacle_positions.2: No pair-to-modulus map is required; every squarefree integer has a unique largest-prime parent, and all multiplicities remain visible in the operator norm.
obstacle_positions.3: The norm is taken on precisely the kernel-sanctioned backward window at X=(y+1)²−1, never on a generic-x average.
obstacle_positions.4: There is no primorial or full wheel modulus; the only packets are ordinary prime-size ranges p≤X.
obstacle_positions.5: The proposed gain is not sieve-only: it depends on the linear sign identity μ(pr)=−μ(r) and a signed spectral gap.
obstacle_positions.6: No pointwise estimate for R and no zero enumeration is used; the prime measure and Li measure are compared only after multiplication by the signed Buchstab cells.
obstacle_positions.7: Finite computations are used solely to falsify the spectral-gap model or locate bad modes, never as promotion evidence.
obstacle_positions.8: Individual divisor jumps may be Wigert-large, but their canonical-window L² contribution is bounded by divisor moments; no polylogarithmic pointwise smoothness is asserted.
obstacle_positions.9: The complete-hyperbola absolute renewal remains rejected; this route reopens only the stated signed door through unique-largest-prime renewal and asks for contraction before absolute values.

kill_test: Construct the exact centered largest-prime transfer matrix for canonical blocks with 10³≤y≤10⁵, using rational Fejér/window weights, and compute its top singular value after removing the deterministic Li/affine mode. If it stays above 1+c, or tends to 1 with an extremizer supported on realizable largest-prime cells, the contraction route is dead. Also verify directly that the proposed packet decomposition reconstructs S_y(u) exactly; any uncancelled boundary term larger than O(y·x^ε) kills it.
rung1_version: It is enough to prove a weaker scale-uniform packet estimate Σ_P W^−1Σ_{t<W}|B_P(X−t)|²≪X^{2−2δ}, or equivalently a contraction gain ||T_centered||≤1−η on a fixed positive proportion of logarithmic prime scales. Iteration then gives S_y(X)≪X^{1−δ′} for some explicit δ′>0.
plausible_partial: Prove, and formalize in Lean, the exact a(n)M(min(y,⌊u/n⌋)) representation, the signed largest-prime decomposition, the critical-shell identity ΔS_y(n)=−μ(n)1_{P⁺(n)>y}−Σ_{d|n,d≤y}μ(d)ℓ(n/d), and the deterministic reduction of the full canonical-window mean square to its single zero mode with error Oε(X^{1+ε}). This sharply isolates the only analytic lemma still needed.
weakest_assumption: A uniform positive spectral gap for the Li-centered largest-prime Buchstab operator in the canonical one-sided window norm, after projecting away its explicit affine mode; no hypothesis about zeros, Mertens moments, or generic exceptional sets.
